paragraphs: Menachem. (Menachem, king of Israel, II Kings 15:14.)
R' Ilai bar Menachem: Vayikra Rabbah 1:13.
R' Elazar bar Menachem: Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1, folio 5b. Menashya bar Menachem: Shabbat 144b.

notes.text: The biblical citation is printed as II Kings 9:14; the earlier draft proposed 15:14, but that correction is not adopted here. The additional Vayikra Rabbah locator ד״ג remains unresolved. Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1 contains the Elazar ben Rabbi Menachem attribution in its folio 5b section.

The saved whole Masorah IIKings15:14 verse names Menachem son of Gadi killing Shallum and reigning; this supports the matching15:14 location beside supplied9:14, without proving a lost vav in print. VayikraRabbah ד״ג remains unresolved; the earlier1:4 nonmatch does not decode it. The earlier Berakhot1:1 folio5b comparison is inherited, not newly inspected, and supplied ד״ה: stays alongside it rather than silently asserting that mapping. Personal title markers remain R' where no new exact full-title witness was read. Bare patronymics do not establish one father or a genealogy.

The print (vol. III, p. 889) gives II Kings 15:14 and Vayikra Rabbah 1:13. The supplied Hebrew transcription has 9:14 and the further marker ד״ג, which account for the different citations in the earlier notes. II Kings 15:14 names Menachem son of Gadi, and Vayikra Rabbah 1:13 names Rabbi Ilai bar Menachem. Sotah 16a has Isi ben Menachem. In the Vilna 5b section of Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:1, Rabbi Pinchas reports in the name of Rabbi Elazar beRabbi Menachem. Shabbat 144b uses both bar and ben for Menashya when discussing his household’s practice of squeezing pomegranates. These notices give individual patronymics without identifying a common father.
